core_obligations: Set up the induction (proof lines 2304-2320): over a regular local ring of dimension two in characteristic p the top relative differentials form an invertible module serving as a dualizing module, as does the corresponding module of each term of the sequence; given a map for one term and a blowup of a closed point, duality identifies a map on the new term with a map of derived pushforwards into the previous term, so it suffices to produce such a map.

Compute the relative differentials of the blowup (proof lines 2320-2334): the two top relative differential modules are invertible by a lemma on reflexive modules over regular surfaces, and the local computation of the relative differentials of the blowup together with the wedge of the resulting short exact sequence shows that the new top module is either the pullback of the previous one or that pullback twisted by the exceptional divisor.

Conclude (proof lines 2334-2342): in both cases the cohomology computation for a point blowup gives that the first derived pushforward of the new top module vanishes and its zeroth pushforward is the previous top module, so the required map exists and the induction is complete, providing the comparison map for every term of the sequence.
proof_roadmap: Use duality to replace the required map by a map of derived pushforwards along the blowup.
Compute the top relative differentials of a point blowup up to a twist by the exceptional divisor.
Apply the cohomology computation of a point blowup to identify the pushforwards and finish the induction.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a regular local ring of dimension two in characteristic p with a subring over which the relative differentials are free of finite rank, every sequence of point blowups admits a comparison map from the double dual of the top relative differentials to the dualizing module, extending the identification in the generic point (statement lines 2290-2302). The proof (proof lines 2304-2346) uses duality to reduce to a map of derived pushforwards, computes the behaviour of the top relative differentials under a point blowup, and applies the cohomology computation for such a blowup to finish the induction. H3: an inductive construction with a local computation, written out in full.
